title: Finding
description: A single evidence-backed assertion about an observed egress entity. A blind spot is not a Finding; it is counted in the coverage statement.

schema_version.description: MAJOR.MINOR. Three segment semver is not used.

finding_id.description: Deterministic, content addressed. blake3 of kind, source, primary_ref and detector.rule_id. Carries no line number.

kind.description: Type of the finding. The last four are produced only by reconciliation.

source.description: Detection source. The only kebab-case enum in the contract set, fixed by ADR-006.

confidence.description: Heuristic matches may only be suspect, never confirmed.

provider_ref.description: Provider identity. The value unknown is valid and must not be hidden.

detector_severity.description: Detector opinion. Not a verdict; PASS/WARN/FAIL belongs to policy.

egress_kind.description: Functional class of the egress, sourced from rule files. Deliberately not a closed enum in v1.

declared_target.description: Where this finding says the call goes. One of the two fields the reconciliation join compares; without it target_drift is derivable in a unit test and unproducible in the pipeline. Absent when nothing established a destination, which is a different fact from an empty host. No field here enters the finding_id: a base url edited in a config must not turn one finding into a different finding.

host.description: Host as the source wrote it, minus scheme, credentials and path. Credentials are dropped rather than carried: a base url with a token in it is ordinary code, and a report that copied it would publish the secret this tool exists to keep in place. Case is preserved so a reader sees what is in the file; the join folds case away before comparing.

port.description: Absent when the value named no port. Never defaulted to 443: a port that was never written is a different fact from one written as 443, and only the second is evidence of anything.

operation.description: Method or endpoint invoked, in the same spelling egress-event.schema.json fixes, because the join compares the two directly. Absent when nothing named one, which drops the join to a weaker key rather than letting unknown match unknown.

refs.description: Observation entities this finding is attached to. The first element, after ref_type ordering, feeds the identity.

evidence.description: Raw evidence references. A finding without evidence is invalid at schema level.

location.description: Display only. No field here enters the finding_id computation.

path.description: Relative to the repository root. Absolute paths are rejected.

related_finding_ids.description: Ascending order. Grouping is expressed here, not by a parent entity.

data_sources.description: Who saw this. Carries no timestamp: a wall clock value in the body would break byte identical reruns.
